author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire colleges and universities generated an estimated $17.1 billion in statewide economic activity and supported 114,262 jobs, according to a 2025 report from the New Hampshire College and University Council cited by the Concord Monitor. The report also attributed $636 million in state and local tax revenue to the higher-education sector.

The statewide picture spans 22 institutions serving more than 320,000 students, including online enrollment, with roughly 66,000 students based in New Hampshire. Enrollment is not moving evenly. The University of New Hampshire reported 2,471 first-year deposits for its incoming class, nearly 4% above last year, while out-of-state deposits rose 7% and in-state deposits remained steady.

Smaller campuses continue to face pressure. Keene State College enrollment has declined from about 5,000 students in 2015 to roughly 2,800 this year, and the school is addressing a $3.3 million deficit with staffing reductions. New Hampshire also ranks last nationally in public higher-education funding, while the current state budget reduces four-year public-campus support by 14%. Community-college early-college programs now serve more than 11,000 students annually and receive $3 million in state support.
dek: A new statewide assessment puts higher education's economic impact at $17.1 billion while highlighting sharply different enrollment trends across campuses.
headline: New Hampshire colleges report $17.1 billion impact amid enrollment shifts
